test.title: A book you read that you found interesting

document.cue: Describe a book you read that you found interesting.

text: The book I'd like to describe is 'Sapiens' by Yuval Noah Harari. I read it about a year ago, mainly on long bus journeys to university, and I remember missing my stop at least twice because I was so absorbed in it.

It's a non-fiction book that tells the story of humankind, from the first humans in Africa to the present day. It covers huge topics like the invention of farming, money and religion, but it's written in a very simple, conversational style, so you never feel as if you're reading a textbook.

One idea that really struck me was that money only works because millions of strangers agree to trust it. I'd never thought about it that way before. After that chapter I kept annoying my friends by asking them why they believed a piece of paper was worth anything.

I found it interesting because it made me question things I'd always taken for granted. Not everything in it is convincing — some historians say the author simplifies too much — but even the parts I disagreed with made me think and look for other sources.
It's the kind of book that changes how you see ordinary things, and I've already recommended it to half my class.
